name: Titanium.Platform
summary:
The top-level Platform module.  The Platform module is used to access the device's platform-related
functionality.

examples.title: Battery Event Example

properties.name: address
properties.summary: System's WIFI IP address. No other network types are supported.

properties.name: architecture
properties.summary: System's processor architecture.

properties.name: availableMemory
properties.summary: System's unused memory, measured in bytes.

properties.name: BATTERY_STATE_CHARGING
properties.summary: Constant to indicate that the system is plugged in and currently being charged.

properties.name: BATTERY_STATE_FULL
properties.summary: Constant to indicate that the battery is fully charged.

properties.name: BATTERY_STATE_UNKNOWN
properties.summary: Constant to indicate that the battery state is not known or monitoring is disabled.

properties.name: BATTERY_STATE_UNPLUGGED
properties.summary: Constant to indicate that the system is unplugged.

properties.name: batteryLevel
properties.summary:
Battery level in percent, accessible only when `batteryMonitoring` is enabled. Measured
in 5% increments on iPhone/iPad.

properties.name: batteryMonitoring
properties.summary: Determines whether battery monitoring is enabled.

properties.name: batteryState
properties.summary: Indicates the state of the battery. Accessible only when `batteryMonitoring` is enabled.

properties.name: displayCaps
properties.summary: Returns the DisplayCaps object.
properties.description:
Note that the `displayCaps` property begins with a lowercase letter, which differentiates it
from the `DisplayCaps` object that it returns.

properties.name: id
properties.summary: Applications's globally-unique ID (UUID).
properties.description:
On Android, this may be the UDID (unique device ID). For iOS, this
is a unique identifier for this install of the application.

Previously on iOS this may have been a UDID, but access to
this has been restricted by Apple. For more information, see
[UUID Article on NSHipster](http://nshipster.com/uuid-udid-unique-identifier/)
documentation.

To use a UUID across different applications of the same vendor,
use [Titanium.Platform.identifierForVendor](api:Titanium.Platform#identifierForVendor) instead.

To use a UUID for tracking / advertising purposes,
use [Titanium.Platform.identifierForAdvertising](api:Titanium.Platform#identifierForAdvertising) instead.

properties.name: identifierForAdvertising
properties.summary: An alphanumeric string unique to each device, used only for serving advertisements.
properties.description:
Unlike the [Titanium.Platform.identifierForVendor](api:Titanium.Platform#identifierForVendor) property, the same
value is returned to all vendors. This identifier may change, for example,
if the user erases the device, so you should not cache it.

In iOS 10.0 and later, the value of this property is all zeroes when the
user has limited ad tracking.

If the value is `null`, wait and get the value again later. This happens,
for example, after the device has been restarted but before the user has
unlocked the device.

properties.name: identifierForVendor
properties.summary: An alphanumeric string that uniquely identifies a device to the app's vendor.
properties.description:
The value of this property is the same for apps that come from the same
vendor running on the same device. A different value is returned for apps
on the same device that come from different vendors, and for apps on
different devices regardless of vendor. See the [Apple docs](https://developer.apple.com/reference/uikit/uidevice/1620059-identifierforvendor) for more infos.

properties.name: isAdvertisingTrackingEnabled
properties.summary: A Boolean value that indicates whether the user has limited ad tracking.
properties.description:
Check the value of this property before performing any advertising tracking.
If the value is false, use the advertising identifier only for the following
purposes: frequency capping, attribution, conversion events, estimating the
number of unique users, advertising fraud detection, and debugging.

properties.name: isTranslatedBinaryOnAppleSilicon
properties.summary:
A Boolean value that indicates whether the current app is running as a translated
binary using Rosetta on an Apple Silicon device.
properties.description:
Use this utility property to guard API's that may not be available on a non-iOS
device, e.g. motion activity or some authorization components.

properties.name: locale
properties.summary: System's default language.
properties.description:
Locale, as a combination of ISO 2-letter language and country codes. For example,
`en-US` or `en-GB`. See the
[ISO 639-1](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_639-1) and
[ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2#Officially_assigned_code_elements)
sections of wikipedia for reference.

properties.name: macaddress
properties.summary: System's network interface mac address, or app UUID.
properties.description:
On iOS, this value is the app's UUID. Apple does not allow
access to any hardware identifier information as it can be used for
unique device identification, which they have prohibited.

properties.name: manufacturer
properties.summary: Manufacturer of the device.
properties.description:
Returns the manufacturer of the device, for example, `motorola`.
Virtual devices return `unknown`.

properties.name: model
properties.summary: Model of the device.
properties.description:
An identifier of the hardware model of the device. For example, `HTC Sensation Z710e`.

Virtual devices will also return a value. For example, `sdk` for the standard Android SDK
and `google_sdk` for the enhanced Android Google APIs SDK running in an emulator, and
`Simulator` for iOS running in a simulator.

examples.title: Testing for a Virtual Device

properties.name: name
properties.summary:
Name of the platform. Returns `android` for the Android platform, `iPhone OS` for the iOS
platform (iPhone, iPad, or iPod Touch), and `windows` for the Windows platform.

This property returns `iOS` for for the iOS platform (iPhone & iPod Touch). For the iPad,
it returns `iOS` for iOS < 13 and `iPadOS` for iPadOS > 13 as part of the iPadOS rebranding
for the iPad. If you need one identifier for both iOS and iPadOS, use [Titanium.Platform.osname](api:Titanium.Platform#osname)
instead.

properties.name: netmask
properties.summary: System's WIFI network mask. No other network types are supported.

properties.name: osname
properties.summary:
Short name of the system's Operating System. Returns `android` for the Android platform,
`iphone` for the iPhone or iPod Touch, `ipad` for the iPad, `windowsphone` for Windows Phone, and `windowsstore` for Windows Store
platform.

properties.name: ostype
properties.summary: Operating System architecture. On Android, this is `32bit`.

properties.name: processorCount
properties.summary: Number of logical processing cores.

properties.name: runtime
properties.summary: Short name of the JavaScript runtime in use.
properties.description: On iOS this is "javascriptcore", on Android either "v8" or "rhino".

properties.name: totalMemory
properties.summary: System's total memory, measured in bytes.

properties.name: uptime
properties.summary: System uptime since last boot in seconds.
properties.description:
**Important**: When developing for the Apple ecosystem, using this API requires the `NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategorySystemBootTime`
property set in the privacy manifest that was introduced in iOS 17. You can learn more about it [here](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/privacy_manifest_files/describing_use_of_required_reason_api).

properties.name: username
properties.summary: System name, if set. On iOS, this can be found in Settings > General > About > Name.

properties.name: version
properties.summary: The operating system's version string.

properties.name: versionMajor
properties.summary: The operating system's major version number.
properties.description: This returns the same value as the [OS_VERSION_MAJOR](api:Global#OS_VERSION_MAJOR) constant.

properties.name: versionMinor
properties.summary: The operating system's minor version number.
properties.description:
This returns the same value as the [OS_VERSION_MINOR](api:Global#OS_VERSION_MINOR) constant.

Will return zero if the OS does not have a minor version.

properties.name: versionPatch
properties.summary: The operating system's patch version number.
properties.description:
This returns the same value as the [OS_VERSION_PATCH](api:Global#OS_VERSION_PATCH) constant.

Will return zero if the OS does not have a patch version.

methods.name: canOpenURL
methods.summary: Returns whether the system is configured with a default application to handle the URL's protocol/scheme.
methods.description:
As of iOS 9, this method may return `false` if you have not added the URL schemes you query to the
"tiapp.xml" file. You can do this by adding a `<key>LSApplicationQueriesSchemes</key>` plist section
as shown [here](https://titaniumsdk.com/guide/Titanium_SDK/Titanium_SDK_Guide/Appendices/tiapp.xml_and_timodule.xml_Reference.html#ios9-security-and-canopenurl).

As of Android 11, this method may return `false` if you have not added the URL schemes to a `<queries/>`
manifest section in the "tiapp.xml" file. Google documents examples how to do
this [here](https://developer.android.com/preview/privacy/package-visibility).

```xml
<ti:app xmlns:ti="http://ti.tidev.io">
    <android>
        <manifest xmlns:android="http://schemas.android.com/apk/res/android">
            <queries>
                <!-- Allows "http://" and "https://" web URLs. -->
                <intent>
                    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW"/>
                    <data android:scheme="https"/>
                </intent>
                <!-- Allows "mailto:" URLs to an e-mail app. -->
                <intent>
                    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW"/>
                    <data android:scheme="mailto"/>
                </intent>
                <!-- Allows file URLs to local image files. -->
                <intent>
                    <action android:name="android.intent.action.VIEW"/>
                    <data android:mimeType="image/*"/>
                </intent>
            </queries>
        </manifest>
    </android>
</ti:app>
```

methods.name: cpus
methods.summary: Returns an array of basic CPU information for all logical processors
methods.description: This is intended to provide an implementation similar to Node's `os.cpus()`.

methods.name: is24HourTimeFormat
methods.summary: Returns whether the system settings are configured to show times in 24-hour format.

methods.name: openURL
methods.summary: Opens this URL using the system's default application for its protocol/scheme.

parameters.name: options
parameters.summary:
The optional options to pass to the URL handling (iOS 10+). Pass a
dictionary with one or more of the following string-keys:
    * `UIApplicationOpenURLOptionsSourceApplicationKey` (String value)
    * `UIApplicationOpenURLOptionsAnnotationKey` (Array value)
    * `UIApplicationOpenURLOptionsOpenInPlaceKey` (Boolean value)
    * `UIApplicationOpenURLOptionUniversalLinksOnly` (Boolean value)
Read more about the available keys in the [Apple documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiapplicationopenurloptionskey?language=objc).

inlined.name: OpenURLOptions
inlined.summary:
The optional options to pass to the URL handling (iOS 10+). Pass a
dictionary with one or more of the following string-keys:
    * `UIApplicationOpenURLOptionsSourceApplicationKey` (String value)
    * `UIApplicationOpenURLOptionsAnnotationKey` (Array value)
    * `UIApplicationOpenURLOptionsOpenInPlaceKey` (Boolean value)
    * `UIApplicationOpenURLOptionUniversalLinksOnly` (Boolean value)
Read more about the available keys in the [Apple documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiapplicationopenurloptionskey?language=objc).

properties.name: UIApplicationOpenURLOptionsAnnotationKey
properties.summary: contains the information passed to a document interaction controller object's annotation property.

properties.name: UIApplicationOpenURLOptionsOpenInPlaceKey
properties.summary: When the value of this property is `false`, you must copy the document to maintain access to it. If the flag is not set, you also must copy the document before you can use it.

properties.name: UIApplicationOpenURLOptionsSourceApplicationKey
properties.summary: The value of this key is an String containing the bundle ID of the app that made the request. If the request originated from another app belonging to your team, UIKit sets the value of this key to the ID of that app. If the team identifier of the originating app is different than the team identifier of the current app, the value of the key is nil.

properties.name: UIApplicationOpenURLOptionUniversalLinksOnly
properties.summary: When you include this key in the options dictionary, the method opens the URL only if the URL is a valid universal link and there is an installed app capable of opening that URL.

parameters.name: callback
parameters.summary:
The optional callback that is called once the URL is opened (iOS 10+).
Also supported on Android as of Titanium 9.1.0.

events.name: battery
events.summary: Fired when the battery state changes. This is measured in 5% increments on iPhone/iPad.

properties.name: state
properties.summary: The battery state.

properties.name: level
properties.summary: Percentage battery power level.
